concepts.name: IDB Founding and Historical Context
key_dimensions: Established in 1959 — oldest and largest regional development bank in the world (UPSC trap: not World Bank, not ADB)
Headquartered in Washington D.C. — same city as World Bank and IMF (significance of location)
Founded as a response to Latin American demand for a regional institution distinct from Bretton Woods bodies
Role of Operation Pan-America and Cold War geopolitics in accelerating its creation

concepts.name: IDB Membership Structure: Regional vs. Non-Regional Members
key_dimensions: 48 member countries total — 26 Latin American & Caribbean (borrowing members) + 22 non-regional members including USA, Japan, EU countries
UPSC trap: India is NOT a member of IDB (contrast with ADB where India is a founding member)
USA is the largest single shareholder — critical distinction from other regional banks where host region dominates
Non-regional members include Israel and South Korea — often asked as 'odd one out' questions

concepts.name: IDB Voting Power and Governance Architecture
key_dimensions: USA holds approximately 30% voting share — effectively holds veto power on major decisions
Latin American & Caribbean countries collectively hold majority (50.02%) — ensures regional ownership
Board of Governors (supreme body) vs. Board of Executive Directors (day-to-day) — structural parallel with World Bank
UPSC trap: President of IDB has always been a Latin American national — contrast with World Bank (American) and IMF (European) convention

concepts.name: IDB Group Structure: Subsidiaries and Affiliates
key_dimensions: IDB Invest (formerly Inter-American Investment Corporation — IIC) — private sector arm
IDB Lab (formerly Multilateral Investment Fund — MIF) — innovation and entrepreneurship arm
UPSC trap: IDB Lab is not a bank but a fund/laboratory for development experiments — often confused
Distinction from IDB proper: IDB Invest operates on market terms; IDB proper gives concessional loans

concepts.name: IDB Lending Windows and Financial Instruments
key_dimensions: Ordinary Capital (OC) — main lending window for middle-income countries at near-market rates
Fund for Special Operations (FSO) — concessional window for poorest members (Bolivia, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Guyana)
UPSC trap: FSO is the IDB's equivalent of World Bank's IDA — but covers only 5 countries, not all low-income
Guarantees, equity investments, and technical cooperation grants as non-loan instruments

concepts.name: IDB Priority Areas and Strategic Focus (2020–2023 Vision)
key_dimensions: Four strategic priorities: Social inclusion & equality, Productivity & innovation, Economic integration, Climate change & sustainability
IDB Vision 2025 — emphasis on digital transformation and post-COVID recovery in LAC region
UPSC relevance: 'Climate change' as cross-cutting theme — IDB committed 35% of approvals to climate finance
Comparison with ADB's Strategy 2030 — both pivot to climate and private sector but serve different geographies

concepts.name: IDB and Climate Finance: Green Bonds and NDC Support
key_dimensions: IDB is one of the largest issuers of Green Bonds among MDBs in the LAC region
NDC Invest Platform — helps LAC countries implement Nationally Determined Contributions under Paris Agreement
UPSC trap: IDB operates in a region highly vulnerable to climate impacts (hurricanes, Amazon deforestation) — policy linkage questions
IDB's role in Amazon Fund and regional biodiversity corridors — overlap with environmental governance questions

concepts.name: IDB vs. World Bank: Key Comparative Dimensions
key_dimensions: IDB has larger lending portfolio for LAC than World Bank's LAC division — regional specialization advantage
Both headquartered in Washington D.C. — but IDB is not a UN specialized agency (World Bank is)
IDB has higher share of infrastructure and social sector lending in LAC context
UPSC trap: World Bank lends globally; IDB lends ONLY to LAC member countries — geographic exclusivity

concepts.name: IDB vs. CAF (Development Bank of Latin America): Overlap and Distinction
key_dimensions: CAF (now called 'Development Bank of Latin America') is a competitor/complementary institution to IDB
CAF has no non-regional members — purely Latin American ownership (UPSC trap: IDB has non-regional members like USA)
CAF is faster in disbursement but smaller in capitalization compared to IDB
Recent trend: Some LAC countries prefer CAF for fewer conditionalities — political economy angle

concepts.name: IDB and Haiti: Special Case of Fragile State Lending
key_dimensions: Haiti is the only Least Developed Country (LDC) in the Western Hemisphere — IDB's FSO most relevant here
Post-2010 earthquake reconstruction — IDB cancelled Haiti's debt entirely (grant-based approach)
UPSC relevance: IDB as a tool of disaster response finance, not just development finance
Haiti case used to illustrate limits of MDB conditionality in fragile/conflict-affected states

concepts.name: IDB's Role in Regional Integration: IIRSA and Infrastructure
key_dimensions: IIRSA (Initiative for the Integration of Regional Infrastructure in South America) — IDB was a key funder
Evolved into COSIPLAN under UNASUR — IDB's technical and financial role continued
UPSC trap: IIRSA is often confused with a political body; it is an infrastructure planning initiative co-funded by IDB, CAF, and FONPLATA
Connectivity corridors linking Atlantic and Pacific coasts — geo-economic significance for trade

concepts.name: IDB and Sovereign vs. Non-Sovereign Lending
key_dimensions: Sovereign-guaranteed loans (to governments) — traditional IDB lending through OC and FSO
Non-sovereign lending — done through IDB Invest for private sector projects
UPSC trap: IDB proper can also do non-sovereign lending but it is limited; IDB Invest is the primary vehicle
Significance: Allows IDB Group to mobilize private capital — 'crowding in' private investment concept

concepts.name: IDB and Conditionality: Policy-Based Lending
key_dimensions: Policy-Based Loans (PBLs) — budget support tied to policy reforms (fiscal consolidation, social sector reforms)
Distinction from project loans: PBLs disbursed against policy triggers, not physical project milestones
UPSC angle: Controversy around conditionality — sovereignty concerns vs. efficiency of reform-linked finance
Comparison with IMF conditionality: IDB conditions are development-oriented; IMF conditions are macroeconomic stabilization-oriented

concepts.name: IDB's Transparency and Accountability Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Independent Consultation and Investigation Mechanism (MICI) — IDB's accountability mechanism for project-affected people
UPSC trap: MICI is IDB's equivalent of World Bank's Inspection Panel — different names, similar function
Office of Evaluation and Oversight (OVE) — independent evaluation body, reports directly to Board
IDB's Information Disclosure Policy — comparisons with ADB and World Bank on transparency standards

concepts.name: IDB and Digital Economy / Fintech in LAC
key_dimensions: IDB Lab (formerly MIF) is the leading funder of fintech ecosystems in Latin America
IDB's Fintech LAC Report — annual benchmark document on digital financial inclusion in the region
UPSC relevance: Financial inclusion through digital means — parallel with India's JAM trinity and UPI narrative
IDB's support for Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) research in LAC — contemporary angle

concepts.name: IDB and Gender Equality Mandate
key_dimensions: Gender and Diversity Division — IDB mainstreams gender across all lending operations
IDB's Gender Parity Group — internal workplace equality initiative (UPSC trap: don't confuse with external project lending)
Women in STEM and entrepreneurship programs — IDB Invest's 2X Challenge participation
Measurement: IDB tracks gender marker on all projects — percentage of projects with gender co-benefit

concepts.name: IDB Capital Increases: Ninth General Capital Increase (GCI-9)
key_dimensions: 2010 GCI-9 — largest capital increase in IDB history ($70 billion) following global financial crisis
Triggered by need to scale up counter-cyclical lending during 2008–2010 crisis
UPSC angle: Capital increases require member country contributions — tests understanding of MDB financial architecture
Comparison: World Bank's 2018 capital increase ($13 billion paid-in + $52 billion callable) — different structure

concepts.name: IDB and China's Influence in Latin America: Geopolitical Dimension
key_dimensions: China is NOT a member of IDB — but China Development Bank and AIIB compete for LAC infrastructure projects
Belt and Road Initiative expansion into LAC — seen as rival to IDB-funded connectivity projects
UPSC trap: China joined ADB but not IDB — different regional membership rules
USA's use of IDB as a geopolitical tool to counter Chinese influence in Latin America — strategic finance angle

concepts.name: IDB's Response to COVID-19: Emergency Lending and Debt Relief
key_dimensions: $12 billion emergency package announced in 2020 — one of the fastest MDB responses globally
Debt service suspension and restructuring for FSO-eligible countries during pandemic
UPSC relevance: Role of regional MDBs as 'first responders' vs. global bodies like IMF — speed and conditionality comparison
LAC was the worst-affected developing region by COVID-19 — IDB's response scale in that context

concepts.name: FONPLATA: Smaller Sister Institution and IDB Comparison
key_dimensions: FONPLATA (Financial Fund for the Development of the River Plate Basin) — much smaller, 5-country institution
UPSC trap: FONPLATA is often listed alongside IDB and CAF in regional finance questions — must distinguish scale and membership
FONPLATA focuses exclusively on River Plate Basin countries (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay)
IDB is pan-LAC; FONPLATA is sub-regional — useful for understanding layered regional financial architecture
